title: Put a call headset on a child-size mannequin head: boom down, cups on both ears
instruction: Put the headset on the child-size mannequin head: lower its microphone boom, then put it on with each ear cup on its own ear, the microphone's cup on the head's left, and let go.
context: Since remote schooling became common, parents and carers routinely put a call headset on a child for an online class, a tutor or a language app; most adults have put one on someone or themselves. Here a child-size mannequin head stands in for the child. A stereo office headset grips the head through its sprung band: the cups rest closer together than the ears, so both cups are pulled apart, carried over the head level and let in onto the ears together; letting one cup in early drags its cushion down the cheek or the ear and leaves the band twisted. The boom microphone only picks the voice up well when swung down from its stowed position to its stop just in front of the mouth, on the correct side. Unlike putting on worn items that only rest on a head, here both hands hold the cups spread, each about 24 mm out, against the band's clamp and let them in onto both ears together, close to a face.
setup: Positions in mm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top; arm bases at y +305 and -305. Figures marked est are the task's design values (the sim is built to them), not maker data. (1) Head form: a child-size display head with moulded ears that stand out: the Xigaocun children's manikin head for hats and wigs (Amazon ASIN B0BM3QNMWF; listing: head circumference 48 cm, ears protrude). It is fixed to the table on its flat neck base with double-sided tape, its axis at (330, 0), facing the robot (toward -x), so the head's left is the -y side. Only the circumference is listed; its shape (est, the sim's turned sections; the head checks below hold the real head to it): neck 90 mm across to 45 mm up; lower face 116 mm across from 45 to 85 mm; cranium 140 mm across from 85 to 160 mm; crown steps 120, 84 and 40 mm across up to the top at 205 mm. Two ears, 25 mm front to back, 35 mm tall (97.5 to 132.5 mm up), stand 10 mm out from the cranium (outer faces at y +80 and -80, 160 mm apart). A 30 mm red mouth line at 70 mm up on the lower face; its left corner (the head's left) at (272, -15, 70). (2) Headset: a Jabra Evolve2 30 SE stereo USB headset (about US$85; 102 g without cable, maker data). Its cable runs slack to a laptop behind the head (not part of the task), clear of the arms and never pulling on the headset; it counts for no check and the sim omits it. Black band, 24 mm wide; two 60 mm round on-ear cups, 34 mm thick with their grey 12 mm cushions (est). Unworn, the cushions rest 136 mm apart (inner faces), 24 mm less than the ears: on the head each cup is pushed out 12 mm and presses its ear with about 2 N (est), and this clamp holds the band with its underside on or just above the crown (5 mm above it in the sim). The boom (est, no maker figure: a 104 mm arm from its pivot at the left cup's centre, then an 88 mm tip arm in toward the face; the fit check confirms its reach) turns from stowed straight up, where it rests on its upper stop, forward and down about 118 degrees to its lower stop with the microphone about 40 mm in front of the mouth's left corner. (3) Stand: an aluminium desk headphone stand (about US$15): 100 x 100 mm base centred at (150, 0), round post, a padded cradle 30 x 90 mm on top at 212 mm. The headset hangs on it, band across the cradle, cups along y (the boom's cup toward -y), boom stowed up. Checks before the first trial (tape, ruler, calipers, 0 to 10 N spring scale); a part that fails one is replaced. Head: 46 to 50 cm round just above the ears; 150 to 170 mm across the ears' outer faces; ear centres 105 to 125 mm above the neck base; crown 195 to 215 mm up (if the ears measure under 150 mm across, glue a 25 x 35 mm craft foam pad on each ear to bring it into range). Headset: cushion inner faces 126 to 146 mm apart unworn. Clamp force (Jabra publishes no figure; sim 2.0 N per ear, 167 N/m est): with the headset on the head by hand, a spring scale hooked on one cup's outer rim and pulled straight out reads 1.5 to 3.0 N as the cushion lifts off its ear. Fit: with the band on the crown each cushion covers its ear; the boom stays up and stays down on its own; with the boom lowered the microphone sits within 50 mm of the mouth's left corner.
scoring: Sim reads the poses of the headband, both cups and the boom, and the grippers; the real trial reads the video, an end photo and a ruler. The latch counts on every step; other states are read at the last step unless a rule says otherwise. Latch, headset left the work surface: any part of it past the table's edge, or any part below the table top (fell off; sim allows 10 mm for contact), on any step; setting it down on the table and picking it up again does not count (real: the video). Off the stand: the band's underside 15 mm or more above the cradle's top, or its centre 30 mm or more outside the cradle's 30 x 90 mm top in plan; sliding it along the cradle does not count (real: the band no longer touches the cradle, ruler on the video). Seated: the band's centre within 15 mm of its seated place (over the head's axis, its underside on the crown) and tilted under 0.25 rad (14 degrees) (real: the band on or within 15 mm above the crown, centred within 15 mm, ruler on the end photo; tilt by the cups' heights differing under 20 mm). On the ears: each cushion's face centred within 15 mm of its own ear (front to back and up and down) and no more than 3 mm out from the ear's outer face, the boom's cup on the head's left ear (real: on the end photo each cushion hides a 30 mm ring drawn round its ear's centre, 115 mm up on the ear's front to back centre line, so the cup is centred within 15 mm; a 3 mm card slid straight down against the cushion's face on that centre line stops on the ear's top edge or the cushion's rim instead of passing between them, so the cushion is clamped on, not held off; a cup held apart fails). Mic down: the boom within 0.25 rad of its lower stop and the microphone within 50 mm of the mouth's left corner (real: the boom on its stop, ruler on the end photo). Resting: no part of the headset moving 5 mm/s or faster (real: nothing moves 5 mm in the last 1 s of video). Hands off: both grippers' finger zones 30 mm or more from every part of the headset (real: no finger touches it in the last 1 s; a 30 mm block passes between each gripper and the headset with the arms held still). Score 0 if the latch fired or the headset is still on its stand. Otherwise: 1.0 if seated, on the ears, mic down, resting and hands off all hold on every step of the last 1 s (20 steps); 0.75 if seated, on the ears and mic down at the last step but one of those fails on a step of the last 1 s (held, touched or moving); 0.5 if seated on both ears at the last step with the mic not down; 0.25 if off the stand but not seated on both ears (held up, on one ear, on backwards, cups still held apart). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0; each end state falls in exactly one. Nothing reads the order of moves; a headset turned round puts the boom's cup on the right ear and scores 0.25.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Head form, stand: fixed shapes as above. Headset: one loose articulation; band rigid; its flex modelled as each cup sliding straight out along y on a sprung slide (167 N/m, about 2 N on the ear; est), the cups upright as on their real swivels; the boom on a hinge with two stops; on the real headset a stop plus the hinge's friction holds it, in the sim gravity holds it on the stop. No cable (real: slack behind the head). Contact and friction only; no rule moves a part.
reset_notes: Swing the boom back up to its stop, hang the headset on the stand's cradle with the boom's cup toward -y, cups hanging free. The head form stays taped in place; check its axis at (330, 0) and the stand's base at (150, 0). The setup checks are done once per new headset or head form, not every trial; the clamp force check is repeated every 20 trials.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (one arm idle: 0.0 left idle, 0.0 right idle)
